properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for Avoca River to Charlton Town.

  • Moderate rainfall was recorded across the Avoca River catchment during Sunday and into Monday, with the heaviest falls recorded in the upper parts of the catchment. River level rises are occurring along the Avoca River.
  • Minor flooding is occurring along the Avoca River at Yawong Weir, Charlton Town and Charlton Downstream.
  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is currently at 4.70m and rising, with minor flooding and is likely to exceed the moderate flood level (5.90m) from early Thursday morning. 
  • The river may peak near 6.70m Thursday evening.
Prepare for flooding now. Take actions to protect your life and property against potential hazards caused by flooding.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Floodwater may affect Gordon Park Caravan Park, with conditions similar to the December 2023 Boxing Day flood.
  • Over-floor flooding of homes is not currently expected.
  • The Boort-Wycheproof Road crossing at the Avoca River may become flooded and unsafe to use.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road, is possible.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Broken River downstream of Casey Weir to Orrvale and Kialla. 

Moderate flooding occurring at Orrvale with a Peak around 7.8 metres possible this evening (Wednesday). 

The Seven Creeks at Kialla West peaked around midday today (Wednesday) with moderate flooding. 
Minor flooding is expected to occur on the Goulburn River at Shepparton. 
Separate warnings are in place for the Seven Creeks and Goulburn River. 

  • The Broken River at Orrvale is currently at 7.71 metres and rising with moderate flooding. 
  • The river is likely to remain above the moderate flood level (7.20 metres) until Thursday morning.

This Watch and Act message replaces the message issued at 10:30am today. 
Act now - take actions immediately to protect your life and property. Move to higher ground away from the Broken River. 
What you should do:
  • People in Orrvale, Kialla West and Kialla Lakes and surrounding riverside areas, including camps, should follow their emergency plan and locate their emergency kit, if they have one. 
  • Decide if you will evacuate if it becomes necessary. 
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous and toxic - never drive, walk, play or swim in floodwater.

If you choose to leave: 
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications. 
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding. 
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace. 
  • Be aware of any road closures before you leave and plan your route accordingly. Visit VicTraffic website to view the latest closure information. 
 
If you are travelling: 
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route. 
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. 

If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave: 
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated. 
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow. 
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:  
  • Some properties in Kialla West may be surrounded by floodwater, and floodwater may enter a very small number of homes. 
  • Riverside areas and flats will be flooded for several days
  • Floodwater will cover some farmland and surround properties around Doyles Road. 
  • Floodwater is likely to cover parts of Kialla Lakes Drive and Gordon Drive, with many local streets in Kialla Lakes likely to have water over the road as the river rises. 
  • All vehicle & walking tracks within the Arcadia Streamside Reserve, Shepparton Regional Park & Gemmills Swamp Wildlife Reserve were closed on Monday, except for Park Bend off Rudd Road. 
  • If your property is prone to flooding, check the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority's Community Flood Information Portal and download your property information statement at: https://my.floodreport.com.au/gbcma/
  • For full instructions, and more local flood information, download the Shepparton, Mooroopna & Kialla Local Flood Guide at: https://www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/greater-shepparton-city-council
  • Try the https://emergency.greatershepparton.com.au/ to view local emergency information.
